subject: Degraded throughput during peak — request for queueing/backpressure commitment and temporary remediation
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@forgeindustrial.com>
To: Redwood Support <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency and dropped requests during morning peak (10/01)

Hi Stephanie,

We observed repeated elevated tail latency and a handful of "503 - queue full" errors this morning between 08:30-09:00 PT on our dedicated pool. This caused several customer-facing requests to fail and triggered retries from our service. We've attached a small csv of samples from our side (forge_q3_peak_logs.csv).

Can you confirm whether this was an isolated incident, and whether the dedicated pool should have handled the load given our reserved vGPU commit? We're paying for 12 reserved cards and expected no request drops at this QPS. Our SREs are concerned about queueing/backpressure behavior — specifically, will Redwood hold requests or return failures when the internal queue fills?

Please advise urgent next steps; our execs have asked for a short RCA and whether this counts as an SLA breach.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of Platform Engineering | Forge Industrial
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@forgeindustrial.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 10:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: High tail latency and dropped requests during morning peak (10/01)

Hi Ethan — thanks for the samples and the heads-up.

Short answer: we should not be returning client-visible "queue full" errors at your committed concurrency under normal conditions. That said, there are a couple of scenarios that can produce transient backpressure (e.g., large simultaneous long-context requests that inflate KV cache memory, or a brief scheduling hiccup during autoscale/burst transitions).

Next steps: 1) I’ve looped in our infra lead (Rishi) to look at the runtime logs for your pool and confirm behavior, 2) we’ll pull server-side telemetry for the 08:00-09:30 window, and 3) propose a remediation short-term (temporary priority bump or short burst capacity) while we investigate.

Can you confirm the percent of requests during that interval that were long-context (>=8k tokens) vs short? Also, we’ll need your permission to share telemetry with your SREs if we prepare an RCA.

Booking a 30-min sync if that helps: Tue 10/5 09:00 PT?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:45:11 -0700
Subject: Internal: Forge incident — proposed temporary carveout and SLA note

Team — following Forge's report: attached their sample log and proposed steps. My suggested short-term options (to offer quickly):
- Option A: apply a temporary "priority carveout" to their pool (3-day window) which routes customer traffic through a higher-priority queue to prevent drops; no additional cost but reduces available burst headroom for other tenants.
- Option B: grant a one-time credit for failed requests if we classify this as an SLA breach, and schedule config changes (increase pool size by +2 vGPUs) while they negotiate contract amendment.

Questions for Rishi: is priority carveout safe for their current topology? Any risk of KV cache eviction behavior causing tail latency increases with priority routing? Also, do we have telemetry that will show per-tenant queue depth and drop counts to determine whether this is a behavioral issue vs transient scheduling?

I propose we present Option A immediately to the customer and keep Option B as contingent.

-Steph
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:22:09 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Forge incident — proposed temporary carveout and SLA note

Stephanie / Laura — quick tech notes after an initial pass on telemetry:
- We did see sustained queue depth spikes on the Forge pool from 08:26–08:48 PT; peak queue depth reached ~78 requests queued per serving shard for a ~45s window.
- The reserved vGPU commit is at the node level; their reserved cards were saturated but not all were fully utilized due to a scheduling imbalance that correlated with multiple long-context requests starting simultaneously (their logs show ~18% long-context during that window).
- When queue depth passes the per-shard safety threshold we apply backpressure and can return 503s if the request cannot be scheduled within the configured latency SLO window. That threshold is configurable per-customer for Dedicated.

Recommendations:
1) Short-term: enable a 72-hour priority carveout (safe) and temporarily increase per-shard queue threshold for Forge from 80->120 requests to accommodate bursty start-of-window patterns.
2) Medium-term: raise their committed pool by +2 vGPUs OR enable an adaptive KV cache cap for their workload to reduce memory pressure from long-context requests.
3) SLA language: we should offer a tailored clause describing "backpressure behavior" for dedicated pools and a remediation path (priority carveouts / credits) so expectations are clear.

I can implement #1 within 2 hours after we get customer approval; metrics will show the immediate effect.

Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@forgeindustrial.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com>
Cc: ops@forgeindustrial.com
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2026 14:17:05 -0700
Subject: Re: High tail latency and dropped requests during morning peak (10/01)

Thanks for the analysis and options. We want the 72-hour priority carveout to start ASAP so we can validate stability on our side. We also want formal text to add to the contract that spells out: what constitutes backpressure, the notification window before we can expect carveouts, and the credit calculation if drops occur.

We agree to try Option A now. Please also include a short note on whether the priority carveout will affect billing or latency for other tenants — our procurement team is sensitive to collateral impact.

Ethan
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@forgeindustrial.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High tail latency and dropped requests during morning peak (10/01) — agreement and next steps

Ethan — thanks, quick update and next steps: 

1) We enabled the 72-hour priority carveout at 16:00 PT today. You should see immediate reduction in client-visible drops; we’ll monitor the peak window tomorrow morning and share dashboards.
2) Rishi confirmed the carveout is a safe config change and will not materially impact other tenants (it reduces shared burst headroom but does not change scheduling fairness beyond the defined priority window).
3) Attached is a proposed amendment redline (proposed_sla_amendment_redline.pdf) with text for a dedicated-pool "backpressure" clause and an example credit formula. If that looks good, I’ll route this to Legal and Procurement and send a DocuSign link.
4) For immediate transparency we’ve included the support call recording and the CSV you sent in a single packet.

Ask: can you confirm your procurement lead for routing the amendment (name + email)? Also confirm whether you want us to increase the per-shard queue threshold to 120 for the duration of the carveout (we recommend yes for the first 48 hours).

If everything is approved we'll follow with a formal credit calculation (if needed) and a medium-term plan (either +2 vGPUs or KV cache tuning).

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_sla_amendment_redline.pdf, 10-21-support-call-recording.mp3, forge_q3_peak_logs.csv
